rationale: P identifies vehicle braking behavior itself, which must be characterised to evaluate SG-3's prevention of unintended braking. H-3 supports the operational bounds and unwanted braking outcome, while FR-7 supports distinguishing intended obstacle-related braking from unintended braking. P remains focused on braking outcomes rather than incorporating the sensing, computation, communication, or failure-mitigation mechanisms that influence them.
determining_elements: “Whether braking occurs as intended or unintentionally” directly addresses the Evaluation Target.
Straight-ahead urban driving at 50 km/h, good weather, and no visible obstacle or vehicle ahead reproduce H-3's operational conditions.
Braking and non-braking cases are alternative outcomes of the phenomenon being evaluated.
Obstacle-related braking is expressly limited to “within that scope” and supports the intended/unintended distinction grounded in FR-7.
P does not incorporate obstacle-detection mechanisms, controller behavior, warnings, redundancy, or mechanism timing constraints.
